concerns.text: Success Criterion SC-005 ('The total runtime of the analysis pipeline ...') is not anchored to any User Story. Every SC must reference the story it validates (e.g., ‘See US‑1’). Add an explicit traceability note (e.g., ‘See US‑1’) or remove the criterion if it is redundant.
FR-001 references “See US-1”, but no identifier US-1 is defined anywhere in the document. The user story is labeled “User Story 1”, not US-1, causing an undefined cross‑reference.
FR-002 also cites “See US-1” – the same undefined identifier as above.
FR-004 cites “See US-2”, yet there is no US-2 identifier; the second user story is titled “User Story 2”. This breaks traceability.
FR-006 cites “See US-3”, but the document only defines “User Story 3”. The referenced ID does not exist.
SC-001 mentions “(See US-2)”, again referencing an undefined identifier.
SC-002 includes “(See US-1)”, which is undefined.
SC-003 references “(See US-2)”, an undefined identifier.
SC-004 references “(See US-3)”, which does not exist.
The term “User Story” is used throughout, but cross‑references switch to the abbreviation “US‑X”. This inconsistent terminology hampers readability and traceability.

SC-001 lacks a concrete, measurable threshold. It states “statistical power and effect size stability … are measured against the total number of migratory species” but does not specify what power level or effect‑size stability metric is required (e.g., power ≥ 0.8, coefficient CV ≤ 0.2). Without a numeric target the criterion cannot be evaluated.

SC-005 references “the CI runner time limit defined in Assumptions” but the Assumptions section never states a concrete time limit. The success criterion therefore has no observable reference point and cannot be verified.

FR-006 mentions “represent weekly migration centroids as trajectories on a Riemannian manifold and apply manifold‑based trajectory statistics” but does not specify which algorithm or library will be used, nor what output format constitutes a “shift vector”. Adding a brief description (e.g., “use the Geodesic PCA implementation from the ‘geomstats’ library, outputting a 3‑component vector in km and bearing”) would make the requirement directly testable.

The assumption 'The eBird and NOAA/PRISM datasets are free from systematic biases that would invalidate the phenology‑climate correlations' (Assumption about data quality) is factually unsupported. eBird citizen‑science data are known to exhibit observer effort and detection bias, which can confound phenology metrics. Ignoring this major source of bias undermines the validity of any inferred climate‑phenology relationship.

Success Criterion SC-001 measures 'statistical power and effect size stability ... against the total number of migratory species present'. Power is a deterministic function of sample size; using the number of species (which determines sample size) as the validation target makes the claim tautological and non‑empirical. The criterion does not provide an independent assessment of power and therefore constitutes a circular validation.
